endorsements.quote: Investigators and developers should characterize the data-stage, identify the continuity signal on which they rely, justify their descriptors, map downstream uses, and propose domain-matched safeguards.

unlisted_practices: Submit a short continuity statement with existing ethics, data-access, material-transfer, repository, or AI governance documentation for secondary-use cases that meet trigger conditions.

Trigger continuity review only when the data-stage undergoes a qualitative transformation in purpose, scope, inferential reach, or derivative status, not for routine reuse within the original data-access agreement scope.
Identify the weakest continuity domain (provenance, semantics, authorization, or relational standing) at the present data-stage and impose a domain-matched safeguard.
Do not treat a single continuity signal, such as provenance, consent, locality, or model documentation, as sufficient evidence of ethical continuity overall.
Document the absence of a representational route for an affected community as a governance finding rather than using it to bypass review.
Apply site-level semantic validation, purpose review, benefit-sharing, and contestability mechanisms in federated learning governance.
Require funders and journals to request disclosure of continuity triggers and safeguards.
Include derivative-use restrictions, downstream reporting obligations, joint-governance provisions, and benefit-sharing conditions in data and material contracts.
Require explicit descriptor justification, limits on population claims, and documentation of context and uncertainty when using population descriptors in polygenic risk scores.
Review continuity at FDA-regulated AI modification and deployment-change points to detect authorization drift and descriptor sedimentation.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework and governance/policy commentary proposing trigger-based continuity review and identifying the 'Continuity Trap' in health data reuse and AI development.
